page: Microsoft Azure D64d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine within the DDv5 family powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, it offers 32 physical cores supporting 64 virtual CPUs with hyperthreading enabled. The system includes 256 GB of system memory, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX-512 with VNNI vector extensions, AES and VAES encryption instructions, and a local 2458 GB SSD storage volume directly attached to the instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64d_v5 exhibits high multi-core scaling alongside average single-core output. Multithreaded execution achieves strong benchmark scores across stress-ng, PassMark CPU testing, software compilation with Clang, and image processing. Memory performance shows strong throughput on uncached large-block reads and writes, achieving 291.88 GB/sec and 134.9 GB/sec respectively. High-concurrency data workloads yield top-tier throughput, demonstrated by 62.01 million Redis SET operations per second and 51.52 GB/sec static web serving bandwidth. However, single-threaded operations and LLM inference tasks yield average relative performance due to standard clock speeds.

The inclusion of 2.45 TB of local SSD storage provides high-density, low-latency disk access without requiring separate external block storage attachments, enhancing resource efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads. The primary tradeoff lies in its balanced core-to-memory structure and unaccelerated architecture; without discrete GPUs, it is unsuited for heavy deep learning acceleration. The D64d_v5 is well fitted for relational database servers, high-throughput web serving, in-memory caching systems like Redis, build automation pipelines, and general enterprise application hosting requiring high multi-core compute density combined with high-capacity direct-attached temporary storage.

Operating on x86_64 architecture via Microsoft Hyper-V, it incorporates AVX-512 VNNI instructions for vector processing. Benchmarks show strong multi-threaded compute performance, high uncached memory write and read bandwidth, and high throughput in database operations, software compilation, and Redis SET transactions reaching 62.01 million operations per second. Single-core performance and LLM inference remain average. Without dedicated GPUs, its hardware configuration presents a cost-efficient profile for I/O-intensive workloads benefiting from direct local storage. The instance fits high-concurrency web applications, relational databases, in-memory caches, and CI/CD build environments requiring robust parallel processing.
